subject: Request: hybrid streaming throughput SLA waiver for Berkeley Analytics
messages:
From: Evan Cho <evan.cho@berkeley-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@berkeley-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid streaming SLA request for pilot

Hi Karthik,

Quick background: we run an interactive analytics assistant on top of patient datasets (PHI, governed). For the pilot next month we need a hybrid endpoint (streaming responses to the UI with fallback to sync) but our security/compliance teams require explicit commitments around both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec for audit purposes.

Specifically, our compliance lead has asked for:
- TTFT 95th percentile under 1.2s for 512-token responses (median is less relevant)
- sustained 300 tokens/sec for bursts up to 30s, with a 95th percentile drop allowed during scheduled maintenance windows

We understand Redwood’s hosted defaults favor best-effort streaming. Can you confirm whether this can be added as an SLA carveout for the pilot (or recommend a hybrid Dedicated -> hosted fallback), and what evidence we should provide (load traces, example prompt sizes, or signed runbooks)?

Attaching a short latency sample from our front-end (latency_test_run1) — it's anonymized and synthetic.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Cho
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Berkeley Analytics
(Attachment: latency_test_report_berkeley-run1.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@berkeley-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid streaming SLA request for pilot

Hi Evan — thanks for the detail and the sample. This is the right ask to bring to the SLA/ops table. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we scope a realistic carveout: 

1) When you say "sustained 300 tokens/sec" — is that per user session (single websocket) or aggregate across the pilot (many concurrent sessions)?
2) Typical output length distribution: most responses are ~150–300 tokens, with occasional 512-token summaries (we can handle tail cases differently).
3) Are you open to a conditional approach: we can promise the TTFT 95th <= 1.2s for streaming when requests fall under profile X (pinned model v1.3, quantized runtime, and prefix caching enabled); for larger tails we propose deterministic fallback to non-streaming with a negotiated token/sec SLA on the dedicated path.

I'll loop in Technical Ops and Legal to draft an amendment. For next steps please: upload a 24-hour sample of request headers+payload sizes (scrubbed) and a brief runbook of your maintenance windows.

Putting a redline together now — sending to you and cc'ing my colleagues for their input.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: request_received_stub.txt)

From: Evan Cho <evan.cho@berkeley-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid streaming SLA request for pilot

Karthik — thanks. Answers inline: 

1) The 300 tokens/sec target is aggregate per deployment (expected concurrency ~20–30 sessions). We care about the per-session experience too; single-session bursts are lower (~50–80 tokens/sec typical).
2) Confirmed distribution — most responses 150–300, ~5% above 400, <1% at 512.
3) Conditional approach sounds reasonable; the compliance team prefers a documented fallback and explicit monitoring/alerting tied to the SLA.

I've uploaded a 24hr scrubbed trace and our maintenance calendar to the Drive link you gave earlier. Attaching the CSV sample again.

Would you be able to propose concrete numeric thresholds (TTFT median/95, sustained aggregate, burst duration) and a telemetry contract (error rates, percentiles, and retention) we can include in procurement? Procurement wants a single-sheet summary they can review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Evan
(Attachment: latency_test_report_berkeley-run1.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: recommended carveout terms for Berkeley Analytics (draft)

Team — internal note (do not share as-is). Evan asked for a hybrid streaming SLA carveout that specifies both TTFT and aggregate token/sec. My proposed conditional waiver: 

- Scope: Hosted hybrid endpoint for pilot; model pinned to rdw-gpt-3.4-q (quantized).
- TTFT commitment: median <= 0.6s, 95th <= 1.2s for streaming responses <= 512 tokens when prefix caching and continuous batching enabled.
- Throughput (aggregate): commit to 300 tokens/sec sustained for bursts up to 30s at up to 30 concurrent sessions, provided request profiles match submitted trace. Outside these bounds, Redwood will automatically route excess load to a pre-configured Dedicated pool (customer pays Dedicated rate) with a guaranteed 300 tokens/sec sustained for the duration of the burst.
- Monitoring contract: Redwood emits TTFT p50/p95, token/sec p50/p95, error-rate p95; 90-day retention; alerts for TTFT p95 breaches > 3 occurrences in a rolling 24h window.
- Fallback & rollback: automatic fallback to dedicated path after 2 consecutive breach events; SLA credits only apply when fallback did not trigger in time.

Risks & asks: we should mark the carveout as pilot-only with a 30-day evaluation and a performance review before extension. Legal will need to sign a short amendment (I can produce redline). Also recommend a small implementation window to tune prefix caching on their traffic shape.

If you +1, I'll send this draft to Evan and procurement as the single-sheet summary.

—Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@berkeley-analytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@berkeley-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid streaming SLA request for pilot — proposed terms

Hi Evan — thanks for the traces and clarifications. Per internal review we've drafted a pilot carveout one-sheet (summary below) and attached a redlined amendment for procurement to review. High-level summary: 

1) TTFT (streaming): p50 <= 0.6s, p95 <= 1.2s for streaming responses <= 512 tokens when pinned model and caching enabled.
2) Throughput (aggregate): 300 tokens/sec sustained for bursts <= 30s at up to 30 concurrent sessions, verified against your submitted trace. Exceeding these limits will trigger automated routing to a Dedicated pool (predetermined capacity) and documented handoff.
3) Observability: Redwood will publish TTFT p50/p95, token/sec p50/p95, and error-rate p95 to your dashboard with 90-day retention; we will configure alerts for repeated p95 breaches.
4) Pilot guardrails: 30-day pilot period, performance review, and an opt-in extension to a Dedicated reservation if traffic consistently exceeds the carveout.

Attachments: RDW_SLA_draft_2026-04-22.pdf (redline) — procurement, please review and advise on commercial attachments. Evan, if these numbers look acceptable I propose a short call to align rollout steps (prefix caching enablement, test window, and alert thresholds).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0126
(Attachment: RDW_SLA_draft_2026-04-22.pdf)
